prompt:
An old hand-drawn campaign map spread open flat, filling the entire frame edge to edge (no table, no hands, nothing visible around it): a weathered, dark, stained parchment page from a soldier's diary - dark brown-sepia paper with water rings, a burn mark, creases and torn edges, drawn in faded sepia ink. Detailed pixel art with clean readable shapes and flat tones, matching the attached reference map's style and colors.
LAYOUT (most important): the page must stay SPARSE and calm. The whole middle band of the page (from about 30% to 70% of the page height, full width) is open, plain paper crossed only by a soft, slightly lighter worn road that winds gently from the far left edge to the far right edge with a thin dashed ink line on it - round map markers will be placed all over this band later, so do NOT draw buildings, trees or details inside it. All landmark drawings sit in the top 30% and bottom 30% of the page, small and simple, with lots of empty paper between them.
Depth: the landmarks are small oblique 3/4-view pictograms that get smaller and the paper gets darker toward the right, as if the road leads deeper and deeper into the empire. Left to right:
- far left: a cracked wasteland battlefield (a few broken pikes and a torn banner, a crater, two tiny soul flames),
- then a great walled gate with two towers standing across the road (the gate may touch the band edges),
- then the outer slums (a few clusters of timber rooftops),
- then the brewery district (a couple of pot stills, smoke stacks, stacked barrels, a short liquor canal),
- far right: the deepest heart - a dark palace on a raised terrace with a goblet emblem, the largest single landmark, sitting where the road ends.
Accent: ONLY a warm ember-orange ink, used very sparingly (the goblet emblem and two or three tiny flames). No other colors. No text, no letters, no labels, no numbers, no compass, no watermark.
